seoTitle: Short & Long-Term Rentals in Phuket: Prices & Areas
seoDescription: Rent a condo or villa in Phuket for a few nights or a whole year: monthly rental prices by area, where to stay, short-stay options, renting tips and FAQ.

intro.heading: Short-term and long-term rentals in Phuket
intro.text:
Phuket has two rental markets. Short-term stays start from about 3 nights and are typically booked for a week, 10 days, two weeks or a month; they are priced per night or per week and change with the season, with the highest rates over Christmas, New Year and the dry season from about November to April.
Long-term rentals run for 6 or 12 months and are priced per month. Expats, families with children at international schools, remote workers, retirees and people relocating for work rent condos and villas this way, and owners usually give a better monthly price for a 12-month commitment. A longer stay also gives you time to get to know an area before you decide whether to buy.
benefits: Short stays from 3 nights: weekly, 10-day, 2-week and monthly options
Long-term contracts of 6 or 12 months at lower monthly rates
Furnished condos and pool villas across the island
Time to test an area before buying

short.heading: Short stays
short.text: Short stays from 3 nights are priced per night or week and depend on the season, the property and the length of stay. Tell us your dates and we will send current options and prices. You can also see our [available rentals](/rent/#rentals) below.

prices.heading: How much does it cost to rent in Phuket?
prices.intro: Typical monthly asking prices for long-term contracts (12 months), by area and property type. Ranges show the middle half of the prices we researched, so the cheapest and most luxurious properties are left out. Short stays are priced per night or week: ask us for current rates.
prices.disclaimer: Rental prices are indicative asking-price ranges based on publicly available listings. Actual rental prices depend on location, property condition, furnishings, contract duration, season and availability. Prices may change.
prices.method: Based on our research of long-term rental asking prices across Phuket in November 2026. Only properties offered on contracts of at least 12 months are included, so holiday and month-to-month rates are left out. Each range is the middle half (25th to 75th percentile) of the monthly asking prices for that area and property type. Where there are not enough comparable properties, the price is available by request. These are asking prices, not agreed rents: the final rent is often lower and depends on the property and the contract.

cards.name: Bang Tao
cards.description: A long beach with Boat Avenue, Porto de Phuket, beach clubs and international restaurants.
cards.rental: Large supply of modern condos and pool villas; one of the most expensive areas for long-term rent.

photo.alt: Sun loungers on Bang Tao Beach
photo.author: Raita Futo from Tokyo, Japan

cards.name: Laguna
cards.description: Gated resort community with lagoons, golf and hotel services behind Bang Tao Beach.
cards.rental: Managed condos, townhouses and villas with resort facilities; prices above the island average.

photo.alt: Laguna Phuket golf course with the hills behind
photo.author: Anton Zelenov

cards.name: Layan
cards.description: A quiet beach next to Sirinat National Park, a few minutes north of Bang Tao.
cards.rental: Smaller market of resort condos and villas; calmer and greener than Bang Tao.
cards.suits: Couples and families who like nature

cards.name: Cherng Talay
cards.description: Inland roads behind Bang Tao and Laguna, close to international schools and supermarkets.
cards.rental: Many pool-villa estates and newer condos, usually cheaper than beachfront locations.

photo.alt: A residential road in Choeng Thale
photo.author: Максим Улитин

cards.name: Kamala
cards.description: A relaxed beach village between Patong and Surin with a local market and beach restaurants.
cards.rental: Condos near the beach and sea-view villas on the hills; quieter than Patong.

photo.alt: Kamala coast and headland from the air
photo.author: Roma Neus

cards.name: Surin
cards.description: A small, upmarket beach between Kamala and Bang Tao, with luxury resorts and villas along the coast.
cards.rental: Limited, mostly high-end condos and villas; one of the pricier areas for long stays.
cards.suits: Couples and families wanting a quieter, upscale beach

photo.alt: Surin Beach and its rocky headland
photo.author: Jpatokal

cards.name: Patong
cards.description: Phuket's busiest beach town, with nightlife, the Jungceylon mall and everything within walking distance.
cards.rental: Mainly studios and one-bedroom condos; noisy near the centre, convenient for car-free living.
cards.suits: People who want a lively urban setting

photo.alt: Patong Bay and the hills behind the town
photo.author: Arnaud-Victor Monteux

cards.name: Rawai
cards.description: Phuket's relaxed southern tip with a fishing bay, seafood market and many long-stay residents.
cards.rental: Wide choice of condos, houses and pool villas; one of the main long-term rental areas.

photo.alt: Longtail boats moored off Rawai Beach
photo.author: ADwarf

cards.name: Nai Harn
cards.description: A beautiful swimming beach and lake next to Rawai, with cafes, yoga studios and a strong community feel.
cards.rental: Popular and quickly let; condos and villas within a short ride of the beach.

cards.name: Kata
cards.description: A compact, family-friendly beach town with Kata and Kata Noi bays and a surf season.
cards.rental: Mostly condos close to the beach; long-term supply is smaller than in Rawai.

photo.alt: Kata Beach seen from the headland
photo.author: ADwarf

cards.name: Karon
cards.description: A long, open beach between Patong and Kata, with hotels along the beach road.
cards.rental: Condos and hillside sea-view homes; quieter than Patong at night.

photo.alt: The long sandy curve of Karon Beach
photo.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

cards.name: Chalong
cards.description: Central-south residential area with Wat Chalong, Chalong Pier, big supermarkets, gyms and Muay Thai camps.
cards.rental: Houses and villas with gardens at good value; no swimming beach, a central base for the south.

cards.name: Phuket Town
cards.description: The island's commercial and cultural centre, with the Old Town, hospitals, schools and local markets.
cards.rental: Apartments, townhouses and houses, generally the lowest rents on the island; beaches are 20-30 minutes away.
cards.suits: People working in town, local life lovers

photo.author: Ryomaandres

guide.heading: What you need to know before renting
guide.note: General information, not legal advice. Items marked "Law" are legal requirements; "Common practice" describes what is usual but negotiable. Check anything important with a lawyer before signing.

items.title: Contract length
items.text: Most long-term agreements are for 6 or 12 months; shorter terms usually cost more per month.

items.title: Short stays under 30 days
items.text: Thai hotel licensing rules can apply when a home is rented for less than 30 days at a time. For short stays, ask how the property is operated, and check the house rules of condominium buildings, some of which do not allow daily or weekly rentals.

items.title: Written agreement
items.text: Under the Civil and Commercial Code a lease of immovable property needs written evidence signed by the party liable to be enforceable in court; a lease longer than 3 years must be in writing and registered to be enforceable beyond 3 years. Keep a signed copy.

items.title: Key terms to check
items.text: Rent and payment date, what is included (common fees, internet, cleaning, garden and pool care), utilities rates, deposit amount and return conditions, pet rules, maximum occupants and who pays for repairs.

items.title: Renewal and notice
items.text: Renewal terms and rent increases should be written into the contract. A 30-day written notice before the end of the term is a common arrangement, but it is not a fixed legal rule for every lease.

items.title: Early termination
items.text: If you leave before the end of the term, many contracts allow the owner to keep part or all of the deposit. Landlords renting out 5 or more units are subject to a government notification on residential leases (2018, revised 2019) with additional rules; most private condo or villa owners are not covered. Agree on early-exit terms in writing and have them checked.

items.title: Usual arrangement
items.text: For long-term rentals a security deposit of one to two months' rent plus the first month's rent in advance is common, paid when the contract is signed.

items.title: Professional landlords
items.text: For operators renting 5 or more units, the residential lease notification limits deposits and requires their return at the end of the lease, with permitted deductions. Ask whether the landlord is covered and check the current rules with a lawyer.

items.title: Refund and deductions
items.text: Deposits are normally returned after the final inspection, once utility bills are settled. Deductions are made for unpaid bills and damage beyond normal wear and tear, which is why photos at check-in matter.

items.title: How they are charged
items.text: In most long-term rentals electricity and water are paid by the tenant on top of the rent, based on meter readings. Some owners charge the official utility rate and others a higher fixed rate per unit, so ask for the rate before signing.

items.title: Rates for professional landlords
items.text: For landlords covered by the residential lease notification, utility charges may not exceed the rates set by the authorities. Ask how the rate is calculated.

items.title: Avoiding surprises
items.text: Record the meter readings with photos on move-in day, ask for the previous months' bills, and remember that air-conditioning and pool pumps drive most of the cost in a villa.

items.title: Included or not
items.text: Many condos and villas include a home internet connection in the rent; others leave it to the tenant. Check the speed and the provider before signing, especially if you work from home.

items.title: Installation
items.text: If you need a new line, installation is often free or low cost with a 12-month package, but it may require a contract in your name; agree who pays for it.

items.title: Owner responsibilities
items.text: Owners usually pay for structural repairs, broken appliances supplied with the property (unless damaged by the tenant) and major problems such as leaks.

items.title: Tenant responsibilities
items.text: Tenants usually pay for minor items such as light bulbs and day-to-day care. In villas the contract should say who pays for pool and garden maintenance.

items.title: Air conditioning
items.text: Air-conditioners should be cleaned regularly (often every 3 to 6 months in Phuket's humidity); agree in the contract who arranges and pays for it.

items.title: Reporting damage
items.text: Report problems in writing (a message is enough) with photos, so there is a record of when the issue started.

items.title: Residence notification
items.text: The owner or landlord must report a foreign tenant's place of residence to Immigration within 24 hours (Form TM30, Immigration Act section 38). Ask the landlord to confirm it has been filed; you may need the receipt for visa extensions and 90-day reports.

faq.question: How much does it cost to rent a property in Phuket?
faq.answer: It depends mostly on the area and size. In our November 2026 research, typical asking rents on a 12-month contract for a studio or 1-bedroom condo ran from about THB 15,000-20,000 a month in Phuket Town to THB 30,000-70,000 in Bang Tao, Layan and Laguna. Short stays are priced per night or week. See the [price table](/rent/#rental-prices) for every area.

faq.question: What is the minimum rental period in Phuket?
faq.answer: Short stays usually start from about 3 nights, and many guests book a week, 10 days, two weeks or a month. Long-term rentals are agreed for 6 or 12 months and are priced per month. Over Christmas and New Year some owners ask for a longer minimum stay.

faq.question: Can I rent a property in Phuket for a few days or weeks?
faq.answer: Yes. Short stays from about 3 nights are possible, and weekly, 10-day and two-week stays are common. Prices are per night or week and depend on the season. Send us your dates through the request form and we will check availability.

faq.question: Is it cheaper to rent a property for 12 months?
faq.answer: Usually, yes. Owners prefer a fixed 12-month tenant and often accept a lower monthly rent than for 1-6 month stays, which carry high-season pricing. Our price table only uses listings that require a contract of at least one year.

faq.question: How much deposit do I need to rent a property in Thailand?
faq.answer: For long-term rentals a deposit of one to two months' rent plus the first month in advance is common practice. Landlords renting out 5 or more units fall under special government rules on deposits; check your contract and ask a lawyer if in doubt.

faq.question: Are electricity and water included in the rental price?
faq.answer: Usually not. In most long-term rentals the tenant pays electricity and water on top of the rent according to the meters, at a rate set by the owner or the official utility rate. Ask for the rate before you sign and record the meter readings on move-in day.

faq.question: Can foreigners rent property in Phuket?
faq.answer: Yes. Foreigners can rent condos, houses and villas in their own name with a passport. The landlord must report your address to Immigration (form TM30) within 24 hours, and you may need that receipt for visa extensions.

faq.question: Which area in Phuket is best for long-term living?
faq.answer: It depends on your priorities: [Rawai](/locations/rawai/) and Nai Harn for a relaxed residential life in the south, [Bang Tao](/locations/bang-tao/) and [Cherng Talay](/locations/cherng-talay/) for families near international schools, [Kamala](/locations/kamala/) for a calmer beach village, and Phuket Town for the lowest rents and local life. See [Where should you rent?](/rent/#where-to-rent).

faq.question: Can I rent a villa or condominium with pets?
faq.answer: Some owners and many villa estates accept pets, while many condominium buildings do not allow them under their building rules. Tell us about your pet early so we only suggest suitable properties, and make sure the permission is written into the contract.

faq.question: What happens if I want to terminate my rental contract early?
faq.answer: It depends on the contract. Many long-term agreements allow the owner to keep part or all of the deposit if you leave early, while some allow early exit with notice after a minimum period. Agree on early-termination terms in writing before signing.

faq.question: What is the best time of year to find long-term rental accommodation in Phuket?
faq.answer: Choice is usually widest and owners most flexible on price in the low season, roughly May to October. From November to April more properties are taken by holiday guests, especially in beach areas.
